assessments.reasoning: I reopened the retained original Ada 2022 material. In §9.5.3, paragraph 1 identifies the simple-call form, paragraph 8 places the openness check after issuance, and paragraph 12 specifies queue insertion on the closed branch. Paragraphs 7/3 and 21 establish the exceptional boundaries. Paragraph 12 also distinguishes insertion from eventual selection or cancellation.

challenge.method: Trace an open entry, a protected barrier that raises, and a target task that completes or becomes abnormal.
challenge.results: An open entry selects the call immediately. A barrier exception propagates Program_Error to all current callers across that protected object's entries. An already completed target task, or one that completes or becomes abnormal before acceptance or rendezvous completion, raises Tasking_Error at the caller. Queue insertion on the ordinary closed branch therefore carries no guarantee of a completed rendezvous.

limitations: A protected entry barrier that propagates an exception triggers paragraph 7/3: Program_Error propagates to all current callers of the protected object's entries.
Paragraph 21 raises Tasking_Error at the caller if the called task has completed or if it completes or becomes abnormal before acceptance or completion of the rendezvous.
The provision selected here concerns insertion into the queue. Later completion is governed by the applicable selection, cancellation, and exceptional paths.

The assessment concerns the text of unannotated Ada 2022 section 9.5.3 and its ordinary closed branch for issued simple entry calls. Queue servicing, completion, selection order, and other call forms are outside the conclusion.
The determination follows directly from the manual. It makes no observation about a compiler, run-time library, scheduler, or use of a physical queue.
